full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Choudhury J: One Serajuddin Ahmed, predecessor of respondent Nos. 1-14, brought in the Fourth Court of Munsif, Habiganj a suit, Title Suit No.96 of 1958, against defendant Nos. 1-7 and their constituted attorney defendant No.8 for specific performance of a contract for sale of the disputed land. The suit was eventually decreed on 31 January 1967 with a direction to defendant No. 8 to execute and register on behalf of defendant Nos. 1-7 a kabala in favour of the plaintiff. The decree-holder then put the decree into execution in Title Execution No. 94 of 1967 which was on transfer to the court of Assistant Judge, Chunarughat renumbered as Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1989. During the pendency of this case defendant No.8 died and so an application was filed from the side of the decree-holder for striking off his name. The petitioner who is one of the judgment-debtors thereafter came up with a plea that in the absence of the heirs of the deceased judgment-debtor No. 8 the execution case itself was not maintainable. By an order dated 25 July 1989 the executing Court overruled the objection. Being aggrieved the petitioner approached the High Court Division with an application marked as Civil Revision No. 169 of 1989 Sylhet/626 of 1990 Dhaka under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained a Rule therein calling in question the validity of the order. A learned Single Judge of the said court, by judgment and order dated 1 December 1994, discharged the Rule with compensatory cost of Taka 500.00. The petitioner now seeks leave to appeal from the said judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

 3. We find no substance in the contention. The obvious proposition of law is that on the demise of either party to the power of attorney the relationship between the principal and the attorney ceases in accordance with section 201 of the Contract Act. Defendant No.8 represented defendant Nos. 1-7 both for the purpose of the suit and execution of the kabala as the attorney of defendant Nos. 1-7. The decree having been passed against him only as the attorney for defendant Nos. 1-7 who were themselves parties both to the suit and the execution proceeding nothing devolved on his heirs after his death. Therefore the execution case cannot fail for not pleading the heirs of defendant No. 8. The High Court Division justly discharged the Rule with the compensatory cost considering the conduct of the petitioner as vexatious aimed at delaying the execution case and depriving the decree-holder of the benefits of the decree obtained after protracted litigation.
